To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have shown that word embeddings can be used to automatically generate relevant queries for information retrieval search tasks, and the proposed methods can be used to improve the retrieval of passages describing experimental methods for physical protein-protein interactions.
(i) The baseline query generation approach, which is based on matching the query terms with the terms in the document, obtains a precision of 0.41, a recall of 0.22, and an F-measure of 0.29.

1) the proposed unsupervised approach based on word embeddings outperforms the supervised tf.rf based and the baseline approaches; 2) gene name and interaction keywords identification improves the performance of all three evaluated approaches; and 3) the proposed methods can be utilized in the future to identify passages describing experimental methods for physical and genetic interactions between genes, proteins and other entities
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic identification of passages with experimental methods in full text articles describing physical interactions between proteins.
identifying passages with experimental information about physical interactions between proteins from scientific publications.
the development of an information retrieval system for retrieving text passages describing experimental methods for protein-protein interaction experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methods are promising for retrieving passages describing physical interaction experimental methods.
the proposed methods can be used to retrieve passages with experimental methods describing protein-protein interactions, which can help in the annotation of the PPIs and their reliability assessment.
the use of word embeddings in query generation leads to higher recall and higher F-measure scores, compared with the tf.rf based approach and the baseline.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the word embeddings based query expansion approach is a viable method for improving the recall of the baseline system for retrieving passages containing information about experimental methods.
the proposed word embeddings based approach outperforms the baseline, the tf.rf based approach and the baseline + gene name and interaction keywords approach, in terms of the F-measure scores.
we have developed an approach for identifying passages describing experimental methods used for physical interactions between two proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

using word embeddings can be an effective way of improving the recall scores for the task of retrieving passages with experimental methods describing physical interactions between proteins from full text articles.

word embeddings are a promising approach for query expansion in information retrieval tasks, and that they are not limited to the task of query expansion for retrieving experimental methods for PPIs, as shown in our work.

the word embeddings based method is able to generate queries that retrieve more relevant passages for the experimental methods, even though the queries contain terms that do not occur in the names of the methods.
